title: Resonance Lab
notConnected: Connect to your machine to check for an accelerometer.
accelMissing: No accelerometer found in the object model. Configure one with M955 to run measurements.
overflows: The accelerometer reported {count} sample overflow(s) — results may be unreliable. Try a lower sample rate (M955) or a shorter run.
notHomed: Home all axes before measuring — the test shakes the machine and needs a known position.
emptyHint: Set the options above and press Measure — or load a previous capture CSV.

controls.customMoves: Custom move profile (one G-code per line)

settings.title: Resonance Lab settings
settings.programDirHint: Where generated test G-code files are uploaded (e.g. sweep/belt programs) — kept separate from 0:/sys's own config/homing files. Captured CSV results always go to 0:/sys/accelerometer (fixed by the firmware).
settings.programDirNote: Captured measurement data itself always lands in 0:/sys/accelerometer — that location is set by the firmware and can't be changed. This setting only controls where the plugin's own generated test programs are uploaded.

orientation.underdetermined: Couldn't fully determine the orientation — ensure the X and Y moves actually moved the toolhead and re-run.
orientation.conflict: The {axes} move excited the same sensor channel as another axis — frame coupling (bedslinger?) or loose mounting.
orientation.coupling: High cross-axis coupling ({pct}%) — check the accelerometer is rigidly mounted.
orientation.applied: Orientation applied (I{i}). Add the M955 I parameter to config.g to keep it.

belts.notCoreXY: Belt comparison needs CoreXY-style kinematics (diagonal belt paths). Your machine reports a different kinematics type.
belts.phaseTiming: first run at these settings — establishing the real motion time, reused next time
belts.matchedDetail: Both belts resonate alike (peaks {peakA} / {peakB} Hz) with balanced energy — no tension adjustment needed.
belts.tensionDetail: The spectra share a shape but {louder} carries {ratio}× the vibration energy — adjust belt tension and re-run.
belts.mismatchDetail: Different resonances ({peakA} vs {peakB} Hz) point at a mechanical difference — check pulleys, idlers and belt paths, not just tension.

profile.cleanDetail: Vibration stays near the baseline across the tested speed range.
profile.problemsDetail: These speeds excite a resonance (≥2× the baseline). Quietest tested speeds: {quiet}.

multi.headline: Per-axis resonance
multi.note: The recommendation above already weighs every axis at once — the per-axis figures below are for comparison, or to deliberately target one axis instead.
multi.agree: Every axis already agreed on this shaper and frequency independently.

config.scopeBody: RRF has one input shaper for the whole machine — choose whether this replaces it for every tool, or only re-asserts it each time this tool is picked up.
config.scopeAllHint: Writes the machine-wide M593 into config.g.
config.scopeToolHint: Writes M593 into {tool}'s own tool-change macro, re-sent every time it's picked up.
config.backupNote: The original file is backed up alongside it before anything is written.
config.appendedNote: No existing {code} line was found in {file} — this appends a new one.
config.disabledDuplicateNote: There's also a commented-out {code} line in {file} — it stays disabled, but is easy to mistake for the current setting.
config.restartHint: RRF only re-reads config.g on a full restart, or if you tell it to run config.g again.

spectrum.heading: Frequency response (calibration / excite)
spectrum.body: The curve shows how strongly the toolhead vibrates at each frequency while it is driven across the band. Each hump is a resonance; the tallest one limits print quality. The recommended input shaper is tuned to cancel that main peak — the dashed line is the shaper's response (how much it lets through at each frequency) and the shaded 'after shaper' curve is what remains once it is applied. A good result flattens the big peak without raising vibration elsewhere. 'Show X/Y/Z channels' overlays each raw axis the accelerometer recorded (dotted lines) alongside the combined curve the recommendation actually runs on — useful for spotting vibration leaking into an axis you didn't mean to excite.

spectrogram.heading: Spectrogram (time vs frequency)
spectrogram.body: Switch to this view (or use Excite one frequency) to see how the vibration response changes over the course of the test — time runs left to right, frequency runs bottom to top, and brightness shows how strongly the toolhead is vibrating. A real resonance shows up as a horizontal band that stays at the same frequency throughout; a diagonal streak that moves with time is just the sweep's own excitation frequency passing through, not a real resonance.

belts.heading: Belt tension (CoreXY)
belts.body: The two belts are excited separately and overlaid. Curves that sit on top of each other mean the belts are matched. If one curve is the same shape but scaled up or down, the belts are at different tensions — adjust and re-test. If the curves have different shapes or peaks, the difference is mechanical (a bearing, idler or belt path), not tension.

profile.heading: Vibration vs speed
profile.body: Vibration energy is measured across a range of travel speeds. Tall points are speeds that hit a resonance; avoid those feedrates (or fix the underlying resonance with input shaping) and prefer the quieter speeds.

captures.title: Captured data
captures.hint: Tick one capture to view it, both belt files to compare tension, or several axis sweeps to overlay them.
captures.needBeltPair: Belt comparison needs both a Belt A and a Belt B capture — tick one of each.

results.headline: Apply {shaper} {'@'} {freq} Hz — removes ~{reduction}% of ringing
results.quietDetail: This capture shows no ringing worth shaping — either the machine is already well behaved, or the test didn't excite it. Try the frequency sweep method.
results.applied: {shaper} {'@'} {freq} Hz applied (M593). Add it to config.g to keep it after restarts.
results.verified: Verified with {shaper} {'@'} {freq} Hz: {reduction}% of vibration energy removed.

panel.noData: No measurements yet — open the lab to run one.

runningTask: Running {task} — keep clear, the machine is moving.

cancel.notice: Stopping after the current move finishes — RRF can't interrupt motion already in progress without a full emergency stop, so the machine will complete whatever it's doing right now.
cancel.title: Measurement cancelled
cancel.notification: Stopped before starting any further step. The machine finished whatever move was already in progress.

confirmGcode.title: Run custom G-code?
confirmGcode.body: This will run the following G-code on your machine with the recorder armed. Review it before continuing:

sweep.title: Calibrate input shaping
sweep.blurb: Sweeps the selected axis — or several at once, overlaid for comparison — through a frequency band and recommends the input shaper (M593) that removes the most ringing.
sweep.run: Moves each selected axis back and forth near its centre · all axes must be homed

belts.title: Belt tension (CoreXY)
belts.blurb: Excites the two CoreXY belts in turn (the X+Y and X−Y diagonals) and compares their resonance. Matched belts overlap; a tension imbalance scales one curve; a different shape points to a mechanical fault rather than tension.
belts.run: Moves both belts diagonally near the centre · CoreXY kinematics only

profile.title: Vibration vs speed
profile.blurb: Runs the axis at a range of speeds and measures vibration at each one, flagging the speed bands that excite a resonance so you can avoid them in your slicer.
profile.run: Constant-speed passes on the selected axis · all axes must be homed

axescheck.title: Accelerometer orientation
axescheck.blurb: Works out how the accelerometer is mounted relative to the machine axes and suggests the M955 I parameter so X, Y and Z read in the right directions.
axescheck.run: One sharp move per horizontal axis · all axes must be homed

excite.title: Excite one frequency
excite.blurb: Drives the axis at a single fixed frequency and shows the response over time as a spectrogram — handy for studying a suspicious peak found during calibration.
excite.run: Oscillates the selected axis at the chosen frequency near its centre

move.title: Quick test move
move.blurb: A single out-and-back move with the recorder armed — a fast resonance check without the full sweep. Less thorough than calibration, but quick.
move.run: One out-and-back move on the selected axis near its centre

custom.title: Custom move profile
custom.blurb: Records while running your own G-code moves — for non-standard tests or reproducing a specific motion. One move per line.
custom.run: Runs the G-code you supply with the recorder armed around it

captureTimeout: The accelerometer never reported a completed recording — check that it is configured and reachable, then try again.
